summary: Join our public health training course focused on waterborne diseases. Learn essential skills to combat health risks and improve community well-being.
lede: Waterborne disease training helps public health, environmental health, WASH and water-safety professionals identify risks and protect communities. Participants learn to trace transmission routes, interpret water-quality findings, strengthen surveillance and investigate suspected outbreaks using field tools. They also develop prevention plans, communicate risks, coordinate response actions and monitor intervention coverage and outcomes.
audienceIntro: This course is tailored for professionals who regularly deal with water safety, public health risk, WASH programming, and community health protection.
audience: Public health officers and disease surveillance staff
Environmental health officers and county health teams
Water utility staff and water quality technicians
Corporate EHS and workplace health leads
School health coordinators and community development officers
modules: Foundations of Waterborne Diseases and Public Health Protection
Major Waterborne Diseases and Their Practical Public Health Implications
Risk Factors and Transmission Pathways in Real Settings
Water Quality Basics for Public Health Decision-Making
Outbreak Investigation and Rapid Response Steps
Prevention Strategies Using WASH and Water Safety Planning
Monitoring, Evaluation, and Accountability for Waterborne Disease Interventions
prerequisites: Participants should have a basic understanding of public health principles and experience in health, water, or sanitation-related fields. A background in WASH programming is beneficial but not required.
topics: Water & wastewater treatment and utility management
